note: The seven 2026 state-executive voteboxes that fill ONE SEAT OF A MULTI-MEMBER BODY. The inventory (outstanding-state-exec-2026-11-06.json, tier 2) said these needed a seat-numbering decision first. The decision, taken from the precedent already in production: NO SEAT NUMBERS. Arizona's Corporation Commission is one chamber, one shared STATE_EXEC district on the state FIPS, and five identical offices all titled 'Commissioner'; its 2026 contest is ONE race carrying seats = 2. Every body here is modelled that way, every seat of every body is created, and every seat is seated from the body's OWN roster so the chamber is whole.
districtTypeRuling: EVERY body gets district_type STATE_EXEC, including the two education boards. district_type is a ROUTING KEY, not a taxonomy label: buildStatewideQuery admits only NATIONAL_UPPER, NATIONAL_EXEC, STATE_EXEC, NATIONAL_JUDICIAL and JUDICIAL by type, and STATE_BOARD / STATE_BOARD_EDUCATION reach a voter only through a geofence join keyed on a specific mtfcc (X0003 Utah, X-CA-SBOE California, G5220 for DC). Michigan's State Board of Education is elected statewide at large and has no sub-state polygon, so filing it under STATE_BOARD_EDUCATION would have made all eight members unreachable from every Michigan address.
raceAttachment: A race attaches to ONE office. For each body the race is attached to the office of the member whose seat was actually up, which is sourced per body below - so a December seating pass replaces the right person. Arizona's existing 2-seat race is attached to an arbitrary one of its five offices; this file does better because every outgoing member is named.

contradiction.oha: OHA's own board page, read 2026-11-07, lists John D. Waihee IV as a sitting At-large Trustee.
contradiction.ballotpedia: Ballotpedia's page for him, read the same day, files the office under 'Prior offices', 'Years in office: 2000 - 2026', and says 'He left office on November 3, 2026'.
contradiction.ruling: The chamber's own roster outranks the aggregator, and a certified result is not a fact about who holds a seat. Election day is not a departure date. He is seated as the current holder of the at-large seat Ikaika Anderson won.
